label: Exact CDF reuse
idea: Different branches can have exactly the same opponent hand distribution. Compute their cumulative probabilities once and share them.
detail: All 169 values must match bit for bit before reuse.

label: Active terminal queue
idea: Build a GPU list of positive-probability branches once per traverser, then schedule only that list for later particle batches.
detail: The original first batch still clears zero branches. Sample order, solver updates and numerical results must stay identical.

label: No-tie product reuse
idea: When a warp has no tie mass, compute its identical quadrature products once.
detail: Every particle and weighted addition keeps its original order. Other cases use the full tie calculation.

label: Lossless CDF compression
idea: Store repeated cumulative probabilities once during learning, then decode their exact original values.
detail: Accuracy checks keep the existing format. Direct prefix and full solver comparisons must match bit for bit before timing.

label: GPU time breakdown
idea: Measure how much time the retained version spends constructing cumulative probabilities, evaluating terminals and updating the game.
detail: Diagnostic timers must preserve solver answers. Eager timings explain the workload; they do not count as a speed gain.

label: Aligned probability writes
idea: Align the first cumulative-probability write in every row so a warp writes into fewer memory sectors.
detail: Only storage addresses change. All probability values, direct reads, samples and solver arithmetic remain identical; extra memory and startup count.

label: Cross-player probability reuse
idea: Measure identical probability distributions shared across players during accuracy checks.
detail: Read-only inventory checks exact identity and the full GPU memory cost before admitting a prototype. No measured speed gain yet.

label: Wider player groups
idea: Measure shared probability work across groups of three or four players during accuracy checks.
detail: Enumerate every grouping and its full memory cost. Select groups from the game tree, without fitting them to a particular learned strategy. Inventory only.

label: Shared accuracy-check tables
idea: Build identical cumulative probability tables once for each group of players during accuracy checks.
detail: Exact numerical results and allocation verified, but the complete large run was 41.1% slower. Rejected prototype archived and removed; no deployment.

label: Smaller shared check groups
idea: Share probability tables among at most three players, with more GPU memory headroom.
detail: Retained after three large and three small paired comparisons: 7.7% less large complete time, exact outputs and all regressions passed. Uses more GPU memory; research only, not deployed.

label: Where shared checks spend time
idea: Measure remaining work in the retained shared-check implementation.
detail: Separate probability construction, terminal evaluation and buffer restoration. Diagnostic timers must preserve every solver result.

label: Cooperative terminal reads
idea: Load each opponent probability row once into shared GPU memory during terminal calculations.
detail: Rejected: the first large complete run was 22.6% slower despite exact solver outputs. Archived and removed; C07 remains retained. No deployment.
